cards.title: Introduction to ASP.NET Core
cards.content:
ASP.NET Core is a cross-platform, high-performance, open-source framework for building modern, cloud-enabled, Internet-connected applications.

It unifies MVC and Web API into a single programming model.

options.text: It only runs on Windows operating systems.
It is cross-platform and runs on Windows, macOS, and Linux.
It does not support dependency injection natively.

cards.title: Understanding Middleware
cards.content:
Middleware are assemblies that are piped into the request pipeline to handle requests and responses.

Each component chooses whether to pass the request to the next component in the pipeline and can perform work before and after the next component.

content.text: In ASP.NET Core, the app._____ method is used to define terminal middleware that short-circuits the request pipeline.

cards.title: Dependency Injection in ASP.NET Core
cards.content:
ASP.NET Core has built-in support for Dependency Injection (DI), which is a technique for achieving Inversion of Control (IoC) between classes and their dependencies.

cards.title: Configuration and appsettings.json
cards.content:
ASP.NET Core uses a configuration system based on key-value pairs. The default configuration source is appsettings.json.

Environment-specific overrides can be handled using files like appsettings.Development.json.

cards.title: Summary of Fundamentals
cards.content:
You have covered the core building blocks of ASP.NET Core:

  • Cross-platform architecture
  • The Middleware pipeline
  • Built-in Dependency Injection
  • Service lifetimes
  • Configuration management
